Hi Priya — thanks for the great call earlier. Quick recap and the specific data points we need to size a pilot and recommend a path (Hosted API vs Dedicated):

Requested items (can reply inline):
- Target p95 tail latency for inference (ms) you want clients to observe (e.g., 50ms, 200ms)
- Sustained QPS (requests/sec) and expected daily peaks / burst QPS
- Average tokens per request (input + expected generation) and % of very-long requests (>1k tokens)
- Target model family (open Llama-style / LLaMA-2 / other) or if you want us to recommend
- Region preference / data residency constraints (US regions vs EU)
- Any security/compliance blockers (audit logs, SOC2 evidence, private VPC requirement)

Initial Redwood read on options (will confirm after data):
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, we can run a 2-week pilot with sample traffic and provide benchmark report. Best when p95 targets are moderate (>=80ms) and bursty traffic is tolerable via autoscaling.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Recommended when sustained QPS is high (we usually start recommending >=120-150 QPS sustained) or where strict p95 SLAs (<50ms) are required.

Next steps: please send the numbers above. I attached a short benchmark template so you can populate sample payload sizes and QPS expectations. Once we have that we’ll propose (a) pilot configuration, (b) timeline and (c) rough cost ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated.

Attachment: quickcart_benchmark_template.csv (CSV template for QPS/tokens)

Kimberly / Ben — internal note to help scope the recommendation given Priya's numbers. Please keep private (reply-all when ready to share).

Key observations:
- With avg ~200 tokens/request and 40 QPS sustained, Hosted pilot should be trivial to validate. The burst to 220 QPS is the hard part: autoscaling can absorb short bursts but tail p95 may jump. We should run a synthetic burst test to verify mitigation.
- For p95 ~60ms target on common models (7B/13B quantized), expect ~40–90ms on our Hosted fleet depending on sequence length and batchability. If QuickCart needs consistent <50ms p95 under burst, Dedicated (pinned GPUs + lower-microservice contention) is likely required.
- Optimizations to propose in pilot: prefix/KV caching for common request paths (reduces compute), request grouping via continuous batching (helps throughput at cost of a few ms packing latency), and a small model quantization profile (int8) for Dedicated if they want the best cost/latency tradeoff.

Recommendation (preliminary):
- Run a 10–14 day Hosted pilot with focused burst simulation. If pilot shows sustained peak >120 QPS or p95 consistently <50ms is required, recommend moving to Dedicated and reserve a pool sized for peak concurrency.

I can draft the config and a bench script (wrk-like) to emulate the promo bursts.

— Priyom

Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on your numbers and Priyom's analysis, here’s a proposed path: 

1) Pilot (recommended):
- 2-week Hosted API pilot, focused tests with your most common checkout traffic and a scripted promo burst test (we’ll provide the bench script). Goal: validate p95 under burst and measure autoscaling behavior.
- Deliverables: benchmark report (p50/p95/p99), cost estimate of serving the sampled traffic, and configuration notes for caching/batching.
- Attachments: redwood_sla_summary.pdf (SLA matrix + Hosted/Dedicated comparison), pilot-eng-setup-checklist.docx.

2) If pilot shows consistent requirements for sub-50ms p95 or sustained >120 QPS, we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity. Lead time to provision Dedicated (initial pool + routing) is typically 2–3 weeks after contract and capacity commit; we can accelerate for an enterprise commit.

3) Ballpark pricing (very rough, to be refined after pilot):
- Hosted pilot (2 weeks): nominal usage fees + engineering time (we can include discounted pilot credits)
- Dedicated (3-month reserved): ~35–50% better per-token unit economics at sustained high QPS; exact numbers depend on model and quantization profile — we’ll produce a line-item after the pilot.

Next asks from QuickCart: please accept the attached benchmark template and return it with a few representative payloads by Friday. I’ll schedule a 30-minute engineering kickoff with Priyom and Ben for next Tue to lock down the bench window. Also linking the HubSpot deal below.
